title: One-bit hypercontractive inequality
statement: Let $\rho\in[0,1]$ and let $f,g$ be real-valued functions on $\{-1,1\}$. For a uniformly random sign $X$, obtain $Y$ by keeping $X$ with probability $(1+\rho)/2$ and flipping it otherwise. Then $\mathbb E[f(X)g(Y)]\le \|f\|_{1+\rho}\,\|g\|_{1+\rho}$, where the norms are computed with respect to the uniform distribution on $\{-1,1\}$.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ and $g$ are real-valued functions on the sign set
